title: Redstrike Finding
description: One security finding. A findings-producing skill emits an array of these as findings.json. verify.md (the semantic gate) fills the `review` block; the cross-model adversarial-verify reviewer fills `secondary_review`; the reporting skill consumes accepted findings.

version.description: schema version of this finding (current = 1). Optional and backward-compatible; stamp it so the shape can evolve without silently breaking consumers (mirrors coverage_ledger.map_version).

asset.description: Target host/URL/endpoint. MUST be in engagement scope.

severity.description: DEMONSTRATED severity — what the evidence actually proves, not the best case.

potential_severity.description: Optional best-case severity if a blocked precondition were met (e.g. a confirmed SQLi point whose data extraction was blocked by an unseeded DB). Set this when cvss_vector expresses the potential while `severity` reflects what was demonstrated.

composite.description: True for a composite/kill-chain finding (from attack-chain-discovery) that re-states already-counted component findings. Reporting lists it under Attack Chains and EXCLUDES it from the severity counts (non-additive).

cvss_vector.description: CVSS 3.1 base vector. Compute it with scripts/cvss.py (do not hand-assert the score); the reviewer recomputes and flags drift. v4.0 vectors are not yet scored by the tool.

vrt.description: OPTIONAL bug-bounty Vulnerability Rating Taxonomy (VRT) classification. Stamped only on a program-flagged bug-bounty engagement (scope.yaml program.taxonomy == vrt); ABSENT on an ordinary pentest finding, so existing findings are unaffected. Lifts the VRT determination out of the free-text `impact` string into a structured, validatable field. The `path`/`id` MUST resolve to a real node in the pinned taxonomy (skills/bug-bounty/refs/vrt/vulnerability-rating-taxonomy.json) — scripts/validate.py rejects a FABRICATED path — and `priority` may not be MORE severe than the node's taxonomy baseline unless `priority_basis` is `argued-elevation` with a non-empty `priority_rationale` (anti-INFLATION).

path.description: The VRT path: node ids (or node display names) joined by ` > `, e.g. `server_side_injection > content_spoofing > text_injection` or `Server-Side Injection > Content Spoofing > Text Injection`. MUST resolve to a real taxonomy node.

id.description: The leaf variant/subcategory id (e.g. `text_injection`). Optional disambiguator for `path`.

priority.description: Technical-severity priority, P1 (most severe) .. P5 (least). Defaults to the path's taxonomy baseline; a value MORE severe than baseline requires priority_basis=argued-elevation + a priority_rationale.

priority_basis.description: Why `priority` relates to the taxonomy baseline. `baseline` = the taxonomy default. `argued-elevation` / `argued-reduction` deviate from it and REQUIRE a non-empty priority_rationale.

priority_rationale.description: REQUIRED when priority_basis != baseline — the argument for deviating from the taxonomy baseline (e.g. a demonstrated cross-user impact that a baseline-P5 class does not capture).

status.description: Lifecycle state. DERIVED from the reviewer's authoritative `review.verdict`: accepted/blocked -> verified, rejected -> rejected, needs-evidence -> open (the two axes and their mapping are in verify-base.md). `duplicate` and `remediated` are post-report lifecycle states with no verdict equivalent. On any status/verdict discrepancy, `review.verdict` (the `reviews/<id>.verdict.json` file) wins.

reproduction.description: Ordered steps to reproduce. Wrap every inline payload, request line, JSON body or command in Markdown backticks (e.g. `POST /tokens {"username":"admin'-- -"}`) so the console renders it verbatim as code.

impact.description: What the evidence proves an attacker can do. Backtick any inline payload/command/JSON as in `reproduction`.

remediation.description: How to fix it. Backtick any inline code/config/payload.

candidate_refs.description: Provenance: the source_context.json candidate id(s) this finding originated from (e.g. ["sa-079"]). Lets a finding cite its originating recon/source-audit candidate so lineage is never silently dropped; the reconciliation/recall gate reads this exact field to map candidates -> findings. Optional and backward-compatible.

source_lead.description: Provenance: a free-text pointer to the originating lead when it is not a formal candidate id (e.g. a chain_candidate ref, a structural fact, or an operator-flagged high_risk_file). Optional and backward-compatible.

cleanup.description: Reversion record. REQUIRED for a post-exploitation/persistence finding that planted or changed state (persistence + the AD/credential post-ex classes) — it proves the benign artifact/change was removed and removal was verified, so the mechanical gate can enforce reversion instead of trusting prose. Omit for findings that change nothing (ordinary web findings).

mechanism.description: what was planted/changed and then reverted (e.g. registry Run key, scheduled task, test certificate, added group membership, dumped hash file).

removed.description: true = the change was reverted / the artifact removed. The gate HARD-FAILS a post-ex/persistence finding whose removed is not true.

verified_by.description: how removal was CONFIRMED (the command/observation that showed it gone, or the reviewer that checked).

ref.description: evidence-vault path to the cleanup proof (e.g. cleanup.md or the removal command output).

review.description: Filled by verify.md (the independent per-class reviewer). Absent = not yet semantically verified.

secondary_review.description: Optional SECOND, cross-model verdict — the same shape as `review{}`, written by the model-pinned `adversarial-verify` reviewer (a different model than the executor/primary reviewer) so a shared-model hallucination cannot pass both. Required (gated) for a High/Critical accepted finding or any composite/chain finding once a report exists; absent = no cross-model second check yet.

evidence_score.description: Quantified EVIDENCE-SUFFICIENCY score — the measured accept/downgrade floor. Computed by the `<class>-verify` reviewer with scripts/evidence_score.py from INDEPENDENT components, and used as a HARD FLOOR on the verdict: score < 55 ⇒ KILL (cannot be accepted), 55-74 ⇒ DOWNGRADE (severity drop), ≥ 75 ⇒ PASS. It AUGMENTS, never replaces, the reviewer — the semantic reviewer stays the authority; the score is only a floor the reviewer cannot raise above. COMPOSES with the independent-evidence probable-cap rule (verify-base.md check #2): the score is a floor on the accept/downgrade VERDICT, `probable_cap` is a ceiling on CONFIDENCE — both apply. Optional + additive: older findings omit it.

score.description: 0-100 evidence-sufficiency score from the named-weight components (scripts/evidence_score.py; do not hand-assert — compute it).

decision.description: The mechanical band: <55 kill, 55-74 downgrade, ≥75 pass. A floor on the reviewer verdict, not a replacement for it.

components.description: Per-component awarded points (request_response, readback, impact_artifact, browser_verification, reliability, chain_depth) — the breakdown behind the score.

reliability_runs.description: N reliability runs (0 = a deterministic finding → full reliability credit).

reliability_hits.description: M successful hits across the N runs; a hit-rate M/N < 0.8 prorates the reliability credit and flags 'race/timing — needs chaining'.

probable_cap.description: True when the only evidence is the skill's own log/tool_output (no INDEPENDENT artifact) → confidence is capped at `probable` (verify-base.md check #2). A separate axis that composes with the score floor.

flags.description: Human-readable notes the scorer raised (e.g. a race/timing hit-rate, a white-box code_citation substitution, the circular-evidence probable-cap).

compliance.description: OPTIONAL, additive compliance-control mapping. DETERMINISTICALLY stamped by the reporting skill (config-gated) by looking the finding's `category.cwe` up in skills/reporting/refs/compliance_crosswalk.json — a deterministic crosswalk lookup, NOT a model-guessed judgement. Advisory guidance pointing at the controls the weakness bears on, NOT a certified compliance audit or attestation. Absent when compliance mapping is disabled or the CWE is unmapped, so no existing finding is affected. Composes with (does not replace) category.cwe / owasp / wstg.

pci_dss_v4.description: PCI-DSS v4.0 requirement IDs the weakness bears on (e.g. 6.2.4).

soc2_cc.description: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (Common Criteria) IDs (e.g. CC6.1).

iso_27001_2022.description: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control IDs (e.g. A.8.28).

evidence.description: One evidence artifact. EITHER a vault-referenced artifact (a `ref` to a saved file in the engagement evidence vault) OR an inline `code_citation` (verbatim source bytes at file:line, for white-box findings) whose `ref` is optional.

ref.description: Path under the engagement evidence vault.

file.description: Repo-relative source file path the bytes were read from (e.g. src/Controller/Order.php).

line.description: Line number (or start line, or a `start-end` range) of the cited bytes.

commit.description: Repo commit (or branch/tag) the bytes were read at — provenance so the citation is re-findable. Recommended; omit only when no VCS revision is available (local-path audit).

snippet.description: VERBATIM source bytes at file:line — the independent white-box artifact that proves the code path (copied exactly, not paraphrased).

ref.description: OPTIONAL path under the engagement evidence vault to a saved copy of the citation (the inline snippet is the primary artifact).

review.description: A reviewer verdict block (verify.md fills the finding's `review{}`; the cross-model adversarial-verify fills `secondary_review{}`). Closed object — the only allowed keys are those below.

verdict.description: The AUTHORITATIVE reviewer decision (`reviews/<id>.verdict.json` is canonical; the finding's `status` is DERIVED from this). accepted=confirmed (-> status verified); rejected=not real/out-of-scope (-> status rejected; set rejection_class); needs-evidence=real but a missing artifact the executor can still produce (bounce back; status stays open); blocked=confirmed real but full demonstration is prevented by target/environment state the executor cannot change (e.g. unseeded DB) -> status verified, report WITH a caveat, do not bounce. Only accepted + blocked reach reporting.

rejection_class.description: REQUIRED when verdict=rejected — why. false-positive/out-of-scope/duplicate are clean drops. 'open-proof-gap' = real-looking but undemonstrable here (env/creds/WAF/time); it is REPORTED as a known gap / recall caveat, never silently dropped. Recall rule: when genuinely unsure between false-positive and open-proof-gap, choose open-proof-gap — a false positive is caught downstream, a false negative is invisible.

decisive.description: The decisive rationale behind the verdict — the single reason this finding was accepted/rejected/blocked (mirrors the reviewer's one-line decisive reason; the sidecar reviews/<id>.verdict.json carries the same field). Optional and backward-compatible.

method.description: How the verdict was reached — the verification method the reviewer applied (e.g. re-read the traced file:line path + ran the PoC; recomputed the CVSS vector; two-identity replay). Optional and backward-compatible.
